key_idea: A kept subtree with L leaves is a union of L root paths, and the largest such union is the sum of the L longest chains of the long-path decomposition; any smaller size is reachable by peeling leaves, which never increases the leaf count.
sketch: Keep m = n-k nodes forming a connected subtree containing the root. Compute heights bottom-up (parents have smaller indices, so a reverse loop, no recursion), pick for each node its deepest child as the heavy child; each chain top (root or non-heavy child) contributes a chain of length height(top). Sort chain lengths descending (counting sort) and answer the smallest L whose prefix sum is >= m. O(n). Pitfalls: n up to 1e6 so no recursion and fast input; leaves are counted in the remaining tree (nodes whose children were all sold become customers); root alone counts as one leaf. Stress-tested against subset brute force for n<=11.
